summary: Frontend-only validation completed on the public preview for the new procedural Binary Hands hero background. Cinematic canvas rendered, changed over time, preserved content readability, respected reduced-motion freeze behavior, maintained responsive layout across required breakpoints, and kept hero CTA interactions functional. One minor code-review issue remains: duplicate data-testid strings reused across source files.

ui_bugs.issue: Duplicate data-testid values found in source declarations ('resources-title' and 'resources-description' each declared twice across frontend/src). Runtime homepage DOM had no duplicate testids, but this may fail strict global uniqueness audits.

action_items: Make data-testid strings globally unique for repeated labels (e.g., suffix by page/section for resources title/description testids).
Optional perf hardening: consider 2D canvas context with willReadFrequently when doing heavy readbacks in diagnostics/profiling contexts (non-blocking warning observed).
critical_code_review_comments: BinaryHandsCanvas correctly transitions between cinematic and reduced states using dataset motion state gates and run-id cancellation; no race-condition regression observed in this run.
Hero layering is correct: hands copy remains readable above canvas, scan-line and pulse effects do not obscure headline/description/CTAs.
Responsive checks passed at 320x700, 390x844, 768x900, 1440x900, and 1920x800 with zero horizontal overflow and 48px CTA heights.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Validated on public preview: binary hands canvas is visible and animated in cinematic mode, reduced mode is stable with identical pixel signatures and scan disabled, hero CTAs are clickable, and Infinite/Eye scenes still present. Waitlist CTA opens modal successfully. Remaining follow-up is global data-testid declaration uniqueness cleanup.
rca of the issue: Duplicate testid strings are reused in source-level declarations for resources-related headings/descriptions. Even when rendered on different routes, strict global uniqueness policies can fail static checks and increase selector ambiguity for shared test utilities. Mitigation: namespace testids by page/section (example: home-resources-title vs resources-page-title).
